```{r}
#| include: false
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
survey <- read_rds(here("data/processed/survey_clean.rds"))
canvassing <- bind_rows(
  read_rds(here("data/processed/canvassing_clean.rds")),
  read_rds(here("data/processed/canvassing_revised_clean.rds"))
)
through <- \(x) format(max(as_date(x$submitted_at)), "%B %e, %Y")
```

::: {.lede}
The 1M Conversations About Care initiative, led by
[Caring Across Generations](https://caringacross.org/), aims to shift how the
country talks about caregiving: from care as an individual challenge to care
as a shared one, and from a broken system to one where real choices are
possible. That shift begins with listening. Through a **digital survey**,
**doorstep canvassing**, and **interviews**, the initiative is engaging one
million working- and middle-class families about their caregiving challenges,
their vision for a future where care is supported well, and the policies that
could make that vision real.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Urban's role"}
To bring rigor to that listening: to turn the patterns and themes in what
families say into evidence that can anchor policy design and inform how the
story of care is told, and to show how those patterns vary across populations
and places. These pages document how Urban handles the data and what it shows
so far.
:::

**What the data cover so far**: `r format(nrow(survey), big.mark = ",")` survey
responses submitted through `r through(survey)`, `r nrow(canvassing)`
canvassing contacts through `r through(canvassing)`, and the interview
transcripts delivered to date.

## Two things to keep in mind

- The three tools reach different people in different ways and are always
  reported separately.
- These are the people who chose to respond. The numbers shown here describe
  respondents and are not nationally representative.
